project: Bruno Constant / E3 Engine — Research Restart
context: Restart following a full corpus audit (winnay_research repo) that found the governing equation is dimensionally inconsistent, kappa exists as 6 different values across the corpus, a 12x arithmetic error in Hawking temperature, and the only pipeline run against real observational data used an undeclared, unrelated constant. Restarting with a local LLM to reduce fabrication risk.
standing_rule: No constant or equation counts as established unless it is computed in code with an assertion/test, not stated only in a comment, README, or LLM chat response.

tasks.title: Resolve the dimensional inconsistency in beta_B
tasks.description: beta_B = A/V = 3/R = kappa*T does not balance dimensionally: [3/R] = length^-1, [kappa*T] = dimensionless. No value of kappa is meaningful until this is resolved.
tasks.deliverable: A written derivation showing either (a) beta_B is not dimensionless, (b) 3/R carries a hidden length scale, or (c) kappa is not K^-1. Must survive manual hand-check, not just LLM output.
progress: 2026-08-25: Established that beta_geom = A/V = 3/R has units m^-1
2026-08-25: Separated beta_geom, normalized beta_tilde, surface capacity, volumetric capacity, decay rate, temperature coefficient, and fluence cut
2026-08-25: Added executable tests for geometry, entropy-density cancellation, normalization, and scale conversion

2026-08-26: Added an exploratory, provenance-preserving comparison between the Phillips aluminum heat-capacity crossover and Norowski et al. quasiparticle relaxation; normalized by sample Tc and explicitly not treated as confirmation
2026-11-03: Closed as resolved by outcomes (a) and (c) jointly; the remaining modelling question moved to task 7

resolution.outcome: (a) and (c) jointly; (b) is available only as an explicit, declared choice
resolution.statement: With beta_B defined as A/V for a sphere, A/V = 3/R exactly and [beta_B] = L^-1, so beta_B is not dimensionless (a). For beta_B = kappa_T * T to be dimensionally homogeneous, [kappa_T] = L^-1 Theta^-1, i.e. m^-1 K^-1 in SI, not K^-1 (c). A K^-1 coefficient exists only after multiplying by a declared reference length L_0, giving beta_tilde = L_0 * A/V = 3 L_0 / R (b). No value of L_0 follows from the geometry.
resolution.hand_check: [A] = L^2, [V] = L^3, so [A/V] = L^-1. [T] = Theta. kappa_T * T = A/V requires [kappa_T] = L^-1 / Theta.
resolution.code_evidence: e3_core/geometry.py (surface_to_volume, normalized_surface_to_volume, temperature_coefficient) and e3_core/tests/test_geometry.py: A/V equals 3/R, the coefficient's numeric value changes with the length unit, and the normalized ratio is scale invariant

tasks.title: Choose and justify the physical meaning of beta_B: reference length L_0 and boundary capacity sigma_crit
tasks.description: Task 1 settled the dimensions, not the physics. Before any numerical coefficient is accepted, decide what length L_0 normalizes A/V and what surface capacity sigma_crit enters eta_S = S/(sigma_crit A), each with a physical argument stated before any data are compared.
tasks.deliverable: A derivation in docs/ fixing L_0 and sigma_crit (or rejecting the beta_B construction), with each choice implemented and tested in e3_core/
progress: 2026-11-07: Options set out for the researcher's decision in docs/TASK7_OPTIONS.md, backed by e3_core/scales.py (14 tests) and scripts/task7_candidate_scales.py -> docs/task7_candidate_scales.json. Key results: (R1) any R*T condition calibrated at the Planck point is G-free and equals hbar c/k_B, so the legacy routes mean R = lambda_gamma(T) or lambda_gamma(T)/(4 pi), and the Hawking-route condition lacks the mass condition needed to identify a horizon; (R2) eta_S depends on the prefactor of sigma_crit, which must be argued, not fitted; no single fixed sigma_crit puts both black holes and laboratory matter near eta_S = 1. Post-hoc observation, not evidence: sigma_crit = k_B/a^2 puts eta_S = 1 for superconducting Phillips aluminium at 0.191 K (0.161-0.225 K for f from 0.25 to 4), near his 0.17 K anomaly, but only if nuclear-spin entropy is excluded; it implies a falsifiable size dependence.

2026-11-07: Researcher responses recorded in docs/TASK7_OPTIONS.md section 5: L_0 is a combination (components unspecified); sigma_crit must be argued, not fitted; S_system is none of the named species, being more fundamental (not yet operationally defined); scope is all regimes within the observable universe.

2026-11-07: Decided L_0 = A + D, represented as x = hbar c/(4 pi k_B T R) and y = R_s/R (e3_core.scales; every black hole is at (1, 1), tested). Laboratory matter has y of order 1e-26, so A + D alone makes no laboratory prediction. Decided S_system = active entropy, defined over subsystems with non-negligible heat capacity in the measurement window (docs/TASK7_OPTIONS.md section 6.2); eta_S claims must quote their window.

2026-11-07: Decided the mean atomic spacing a = n^(-1/3) as a third length, with sigma_crit = k_B/a^2 and eta_S = (S_act/(N k_B))/(3a/R) (e3_core.scales, tested). On real Al crystal faces the prefactor is 0.79-0.92, inside the reported f = 0.25-4 band. Task 7 is closed and task 9 is unblocked.
open_questions: How x, y and z combine for systems away from the black-hole point (not blocking task 9)
Cite a source confirming that aluminium nuclear spins are frozen (fully disordered, negligible heat capacity) in zero field over 0.17-1.2 K
The prefactor 1 in sigma_crit = k_B/a^2 rests on a heuristic argument, not a derivation

leads.statement: Both legacy kappa routes reduce to k_B/(hbar c) times a pure number, with G and the black-hole mass cancelling: l_P * T_P = hbar c / k_B, so 3/(l_P T_P) = 3 k_B/(hbar c) = 1310.1097... m^-1 K^-1; R_s * T_H = hbar c/(4 pi k_B) for every mass, so 3/(R_s T_H) = 12 pi k_B/(hbar c) = 16463.32... m^-1 K^-1.
leads.status: algebraic identity; tested in e3_core/tests/test_constants.py, including that G and the mass cancel

leads.statement: Therefore the legacy condition 3/R = kappa T with kappa = 3 k_B/(hbar c) is equivalent to R = hbar c/(k_B T): the region radius equals the thermal photon length scale (the inverse of the thermal photon wavenumber k_B T/(hbar c)). This is not the Wien peak wavelength (b = 2.8978e-3 m K differs from hbar c/k_B = 2.2899e-3 m K). It is a candidate for L_0, not an established result.
leads.status: candidate interpretation; the equivalence is tested in e3_core/tests/test_scales.py; see docs/TASK7_OPTIONS.md option A

leads.statement: For massive particles the analogous scale is the thermal de Broglie wavelength lambda_th = h/sqrt(2 pi m k_B T), which governs the onset of quantum degeneracy in laser-cooled gases (n lambda_th^3 of order 2.6 for an ideal Bose gas). It may connect the cosmic and laboratory regimes.

If sigma_crit is the Bekenstein-Hawking capacity k_B/(4 l_P^2) = 1.32e46 J K^-1 m^-2, then eta_S is about 1e-46 for the Phillips aluminium sample at 1 K and about 3e-43 for 200 J/K in a 1 L sphere. eta_S = 1 cannot be tested in the laboratory under that choice, so a laboratory test needs a different, independently justified sigma_crit.
leads.status: sigma value computed in e3_core.constants.bekenstein_hawking_surface_entropy_density and tested; the eta_S estimates are order-of-magnitude calculations, 2026-11-03, not yet in code

tasks.title: Rename the six kappa values into distinct symbols
tasks.description: Six different values currently share the name kappa: 1313 (Planck route), 1366 (GW route, refuted), 0.001005 (Chajar/tangency constant, dimensionless), 1340e-6 (kappa_lab, unverified), 1.23456789e-23 (placeholder, to be deleted), 1.0e-23 (unrelated toy model). Each real quantity needs its own name before further reuse.

progress: 2026-11-03: Naming decision recorded in docs/NOTATION.md under 'Legacy kappa values'. 3/(l_P T_P) -> kappa_T^Pl and 3/(R_s T_H) -> kappa_T^GW (one coefficient role in m^-1 K^-1, evaluated on two (R, T) pairs; their ratio is exactly 4 pi). tasks.title: Add a BCS baseline for superconductivity comparisons
progress: 2026-11-03: Added e3_core/bcs.py (standard library only) and docs/BCS_BASELINE.md. Tests check Delta(0)/(k_B Tc) = pi exp(-gamma_E), the jump 12/(7 zeta(3)), the slope of Delta^2 at Tc, the entropy balance, the condensation energy and C = T dS/dT. Weak-coupling crossover t* = 0.5147917502752, matching an independent scipy Matsubara-sum implementation to 1e-13. Nine deliberately introduced errors were each caught by the tests.

2026-11-03: Aluminium and niobium summaries now report the BCS crossover. Aluminium: measured minus BCS = -0.0090 in T/Tc, and at the BCS temperature the measured (C_s-C_n)/C_n = +1.8%, within the paper's ~2% point precision, so no departure from weak-coupling BCS is resolved. Niobium: the graphical bracket 0.606-0.645 lies above BCS. An exploratory alpha-model check (not in the repo) moves the crossover upward only to about 0.552 at Delta(0)/(k_B Tc) = 2.0, so the offset is not explained.
tasks.description: Weak-coupling BCS theory predicts the C_s = C_n crossing at T/Tc = 0.51479 (e3_core/bcs.py); Phillips aluminium Table II gives 0.506. Every superconductivity comparison must report the BCS prediction alongside the data, so that only departures from BCS can count as E3 evidence.
tasks.deliverable: e3_core/bcs.py with tests against textbook weak-coupling values (Delta(0)/(k_B Tc) = 1.764, Delta C/(gamma Tc) = 1.43 at Tc), and the BCS crossover reported in the aluminium and niobium analyses

reference/known_physics_reference.json mixes vintages: M_sun (IAU 2015 nominal) was derived with CODATA 2014 G = 6.67408e-11, but G is CODATA 2018 = 6.67430e-11. G*M_sun computed from the two is therefore off by about 3e-5, which exceeds G's own 2.2e-5 uncertainty (quantified in test_constants.py). Solar-mass work should use the nominal parameter (GM)_sun = 1.3271244e20 m^3 s^-2 directly.
